# `tox.yml`

## Inputs

| Name | Description | Type | Default | Required |
| :--- | :---------- | :--- | :------ | :------: |
| allow_fork_prs | Allow fork PRs to run this workflow (set false for self-hosted runners) | `boolean` | `true` | no |
| cache_tox | Cache the .tox virtualenvs between runs | `boolean` | `true` | no |
| diff_cover_compare_branch | Branch to diff against. Empty (default) uses the pull request's own base branch, which is what the GitLab template's hardcoded origin/main meant in practice. | `string` | `` | no |
| diff_cover_fail_under | Coverage threshold for changed lines, percent | `number` | `100` | no |
| discover_python_version | Python used to run `tox -l` in the discover job | `string` | `3.x` | no |
| extra_apt | Space-separated apt packages needed by the test suite (e.g. "sqlite3 ffmpeg"). Empty installs nothing -- unlike the GitLab template, git is already present on the runner. | `string` | `` | no |
| pre_commands | <pre>Shell run after extra_apt and before tox, in each matrix leg. For test suites that need a SERVICE rather than a package -- apt can install postgres but cannot leave you a running cluster with a known password, and the runner user is not root.<br>Deliberately free-form rather than a `postgres: true` flag. A reusable workflow cannot attach a service container conditionally (a declared service always starts), so a boolean would spin up postgres for every consumer. This keeps the setup in the repo that needs it -- discord-bot passes `sudo sh tests/start_postgres_for_ci.sh`, reusing the script it already had for the GitLab runner, which needed root for exactly the same reason.<br>Runs with `set -euo pipefail`; a non-zero exit fails the leg.</pre> | `string` | `` | no |
| runner_labels | Runner labels as JSON array (e.g., ["self-hosted", "oke"]) | `string` | `["ubuntu-24.04"]` | no |
